t: Churchill was a soldier and war correspondent before entering Parliament in 1900, and he crossed from the Conservatives to the Liberals and back, holding most of the great offices of state over half a century.

As prime minister from May 1940 he refused to seek a peace settlement after the fall of France, led a coalition government and built the alliance with the United States and the Soviet Union that defeated Germany in 1945.

A staunch imperialist, he has been criticised for his views on race and for decisions such as the bombing of Iraq in the 1920s, his government's response to the Bengal famine and the area bombing of Germany.
dyk: Churchill had a lateral lisp from childhood and worked on his pronunciation of the letter 's'; he turned the impediment into an asset, as when he called Hitler a "Nar-zee".
ev: Winston Churchill is born at Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire
He is elected Conservative MP for Oldham, aged 25, after his escape from a Boer prisoner-of-war camp
The naval attack on the Dardanelles and the Gallipoli campaign fail, and he is removed from the Admiralty
As Chancellor of the Exchequer he returns sterling to the gold standard
He becomes prime minister and resolves to fight on after the fall of France
Germany surrenders; weeks later the Conservatives lose the general election to Labour
He returns as prime minister, serving until his resignation in 1955
Churchill dies in London and is given a state funeral

f.born: 30 November 1874, at Blenheim Palace in Oxfordshire; son of the Conservative politician Lord Randolph Churchill and Jennie, daughter of the American businessman Leonard Jerome, of the aristocratic Spencer family and a descendant of the 1st Duke of Marlborough
f.died: 24 January 1965, at his London home, 28 Hyde Park Gate, after a final stroke on 10 January; given a state funeral and buried at St Martin's Church, Bladon
f.role: Army officer and war correspondent (1895-1900); Member of Parliament for some 62 of the years between 1900 and 1964; President of the Board of Trade (1908-1910); Home Secretary (1910-1911); First Lord of the Admiralty (1911-1915, 1939-1940); Chancellor of the Exchequer (1924-1929); Prime Minister (1940-1945, 1951-1955); leader of the Conservative Party (1940-1955)
f.known: Leading Britain through the Second World War; his wartime speeches; the Dardanelles campaign; social reforms as a Liberal minister; returning sterling to the gold standard; the "iron curtain" speech; the Nobel Prize in Literature (1953); his record in the Empire, from Iraq to the Bengal famine
